newsitem.title: BELARUS: Daewoo eyeing $400 mln Belarus vehicle ventures.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo eyeing $400 mln Belarus vehicle ventures.

text.p: The Daewoo group is considering investing $400 million in Belarus to build cars and commercial vehicles, the country's minister for foreign economic relations Mikhail Marinich said on Wednesday.
"The size of the possible investment is $400 million," Marinich told journalists visiting Minsk.
"Half of that amount would be used to make Daewoo vehicles and half would support the existing production of (Belarus automaker) BelAZ."

Daewoo, which has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Belarus government about the investment, would build 60,000 sedans and 30,000 commercial vehicles a year, including minibuses and vans, he said.

BelAZ, which specialises in heavy-duty trucks and off-road construction vehicles, has been building Lublin-brand light commercial vehicles made by a Polish company once named FSL that Daewoo bought in 1995.
Marinich did not elaborate on how Daewoo would support BelAZ, which is based in Zhodino. But Daewoo might be able to take equity in the Belarus automaker.
"The BelAZ plant will be transformed into a joint stock company and Daewoo could have a chance to buy shares," Marinich said.
The South Korean conglomerate also wants to produce consumer goods in Belarus.
"We also plan to cooperate with Daewoo in the production of electronic home appliances, such as TVs, TV tubes, vacuum cleaners, video recorders and washing machines," Marinich said.
Daewoo's production in Belarus on a rough estimate might include two million tubes and one million TV sets a year.
"I have seen such a Daewoo plant in Vietnam," he said. "They build TVs, tubes and a lot of other appliances in the same place. It's very compact."
